messages:
alex: FYI, after the merge that went out ~2h ago we're seeing a P95 spike (~2.2x) on text-generation. Tracing shows a bunch of long kernel compile calls and a new autotune selection.
maria: which PR? link?
alex: PR #8217 (kernel-selection change: prefer f32_tile_64 for micro-batches) merged at 1749499200. Rollout metrics show the error window starting ~1749499800.
perf-ci: [bot] perf test failed: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/6821 — P95 gen latency +120% vs baseline :rotating_light:
chen: looked at the node logs — seeing many compile_kernel entries with ~4-5s compile durations on first requests. Previously we hit the precompiled kernel cache.
sam: any idea why cache missed? nvprof or compile logs?
julia: grabbed logs from an affected instance. snippet:
```
[2025-02-06T11:44:52Z] autotune: picked kernel=f32_tile_64 (batch=1, seq=128)
[2025-02-06T11:44:52Z] compile_kernel: f32_tile_64 compile took=4.7s
[2025-02-06T11:44:52Z] kv_cache: miss model=v2 key=abc123
```
alex: sounds like the autotuner now prefers a kernel that wasn't in the cache, and a recent change to fingerprinting widened the keyspace so compiled kernels don't get reused.
maria: can we bisect commits since yesterday? I suspect the fingerprint change in #8190 area.
chen: running git bisect across recent merges. will report back.
perf-ci: [bot] chen started bisect for perf regression.
chen: bisect narrowed it to commit 5b9f7c (author: infra-compile). That commit expanded kernel fingerprint to include build flags; hit-rate dropped from ~98% to ~12% during warmup.
sam: that would explain a compile storm — many processes compile the same kernels simultaneously.
julia: reproduced locally by spinning up 8 workers and firing 200 short requests in parallel — see ~80 compile events and high P95.
alex: mitigation plan: revert 5b9f7c on main (hotfix) and add a temporary autotune pin to the previous kernel profile until cache is repopulated.
maria: yes, and add a perf CI that simulates concurrent warm-start traffic so this doesn't slip again.
chen: opening revert PR #8223 now and adding metrics for kernel_cache_hit_ratio, compile_count, and pending_compiles.
infra-bot: deploy started for PR #8223 to staging.
perf-ci: [bot] re-running perf suite against staging.
sam: long term: restrict fingerprint expansion to only flags that affect runtime semantics; open RFC + unit tests for fingerprint rules.
julia: also propose an autotune safety: if compile_rate > threshold and P95 increases > threshold, automatically fall back to a conservative kernel and throttle new compiles.
alex: agreed. After revert merges we'll watch per-route P95 and compile counts for the next hour. tagging ops for observation.
maria: action items: chen= revert+metrics, sam= fingerprint RFC, julia= autotune guard, alex= monitor+rollback. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — keeping thread live until staging perf looks back to baseline.
